o.text: From Proto-Turkic *ēŋ-ek (“cheeks; jaw; chin”). Cognate with Kyrgyz ээк (eek), Shor ээк, Khakas эк (ek), Southern Altai ээк (eek), Uzbek iyak, engak, Tatar ияк (iyäk), Kazakh иек (iyek), Turkmen eňek, etc.

Borrowed from Arabic وَزْنَة (wazna, “particular weight”). Compare also Persian وزنة (vazna, vaznat, “weight; a small balance; a powder flask”). Such powder flasks initially looked like small weights; the sewing of the gazyr onto the front-garment began only later.
